questions.question: REST vs GraphQL from a frontend perspective — which to pick?
questions.title: REST vs GraphQL (2026) — Frontend Developer Perspective
questions.direct_answer:
REST vs GraphQL from a frontend perspective — which to pick?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser, network, and server contract (headers, cookies, streams)), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** REST: simple, cacheable HTTP; GraphQL: precise fetching, fewer round trips, complex caching, extra tooling.

**Classic weak answer:** Assuming GraphQL always reduces over-fetching — without careful field selection and cache setup, it can perform worse.

**Senior finish:** Frame the decision by team size/ecosystem; mention tRPC as a third option for TypeScript full-stack teams.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **REST vs GraphQL (2026) — Frontend Developer Perspective** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** REST vs GraphQL from a frontend perspective — which to pick?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **REST: simple, cacheable HTTP; GraphQL: precise fetching, fewer round trips, complex caching, extra tooling**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Assuming GraphQL always reduces over-fetching — without careful field selection and cache setup, it can perform worse**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Frame the decision by team size/ecosystem; mention tRPC as a third option for TypeScript full-stack teams**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** REST: simple, cacheable HTTP; GraphQL: precise fetching, fewer round trips, complex caching, extra tooling
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Mental model (flowchart)
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Client["Browser / SPA"]
        UI[UI layer]
        CF[fetch / axios client]
        IC[Interceptors]
        AC[AbortController / cancel]
    end
    subgraph Edge["Edge concerns"]
        CORS[CORS preflight]
        CACHE[HTTP cache + ETags]
        RETRY[Retry + backoff + jitter]
    end
    API[(REST / GraphQL API)]
    UI --> CF --> IC --> CORS
    IC --> RETRY
    CF --> AC
    CORS --> API
    CACHE --> API
    RETRY --> API
```

| **Proof you shipped it** | Metrics (LCP, error rate), tests, DevTools trace, or incident story |

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **assuming GraphQL always reduces over-fetching — without careful field selection and cache setup, it can perform worse** and what you do instead.

sections.title: Key points (memorize this list)
sections.content:
- **Headline definition** in one sentence.
- **Mechanism:** REST: simple, cacheable HTTP; GraphQL: precise fetching, fewer round trips, complex caching, extra tooling
- **Pitfall:** Assuming GraphQL always reduces over-fetching — without careful field selection and cache setup, it can perform worse
- **Differentiator:** Frame the decision by team size/ecosystem; mention tRPC as a third option for TypeScript full-stack teams
- **Proof:** DevTools / Network / Performance trace, test strategy, or metric.
- **Close:** decision rule + sensible follow-up question back to the interviewer.

sections.title: How to answer verbally (timed)
sections.content:
**Open (15–20 seconds):** Restate the question and give the one-sentence definition.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **REST: simple, cacheable HTTP; GraphQL: precise fetching, fewer round trips, complex caching, extra tooling** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Assuming GraphQL always reduces over-fetching — without careful field selection and cache setup, it can perform worse** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

**Finish (15–20 seconds):** Add **Frame the decision by team size/ecosystem; mention tRPC as a third option for TypeScript full-stack teams**, then offer a trade-off question back (“do you optimize for TTFB or TTI here?”).
